subject: Re: Redwood MSA — carve-out for IP rights / liability cap
messages:

Cc: sam.brown@brighttower.com, procurement@brighttower.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed MSA redlines — cap carve-out for IP claims

Hi Stephanie,

Attaching our redlines (BT-Redlines_v3.pdf). The main outstanding commercial issue for us is the liability cap and a carve-out for IP infringement claims tied to the indemnity article. Our counsel is asking that claims for third-party IP infringement — and any equitable relief tied to those claims — not be subject to the monetary cap in Section 12.2. They cite typical enterprise bargaining positions where IP indemnities survive and are uncapped.

Concretely we are proposing:
- A narrow carve-out: “Notwithstanding the cap in Section 12.2, either party’s indemnity obligations with respect to claims alleging infringement of third-party intellectual property shall not be subject to such cap.”
- Add explicit survival for IP indemnity and a defense-cooperation clause.

We appreciate Redwood’s position on limiting exposure, so we are open to language that narrows the scope (e.g., exclude third-party claims only where Customer provides code or config that caused the claim, or limit to willful infringement). Please confirm whether Redwood can accept an IP carve-out in principle and whether there are commercial mitigations (e.g., subcaps, insurance, or upfront fees) that would make this acceptable to your leadership.

Thanks — Kate

Subject: Re: Proposed MSA redlines — cap carve-out for IP claims

Kate — thanks for the redlines and the clear ask. Looping in Marcus and Aditya to confirm risk and commercial options; Monica for commercial fallback.

High level from our side: Redwood’s standard is to keep a global monetary cap on direct and consequential damages with only a narrow survival of certain obligations. Making IP indemnity entirely uncapped is a material shift. That said, we want to be constructive and avoid stalling the deal.

Options we can consider:
- Technical compromise: carve-out for IP indemnity but limited to defense costs and settlements (no uncapped punitive/equitable damages), or
- Behavioral carve-out: uncapped only for willful infringement or where Redwood’s model weights/weights+code are at issue, or
- Commercial trade: agree to a broader carve-out in exchange for a higher committed spend / onboarding fee or a specific insurance confirmation.

Aditya — can you provide a redline suggestion that narrows BrightTower’s proposed language while preserving their core ask? Marcus/Monica — do any of these options map to acceptable commercial concessions (credits, fees, insurance)?

Subject: RE: Proposed MSA redlines — carve-out language suggestion

Team (and Kate),

High-level legal take and a proposed compromise redline below. Goal: limit Redwood’s open-ended exposure while giving BrightTower meaningful protection for IP claims.

Concerns: an uncapped obligation can expose Redwood to unlimited consequential relief (injunctions, lost profits) if not carefully drafted. We should separate monetary indemnity (defense costs and settlements) from injunctive relief and explicitly require mitigation and notice.

Proposed redline (conceptual):
"Notwithstanding Section 12.2 (Limitation of Liability), each party’s indemnification obligations with respect to claims alleging third-party infringement of intellectual property shall not be subject to the monetary cap in Section 12.2 solely to the extent necessary to satisfy monetary awards for (i) reasonable defense costs and (ii) settlements or final judgments allocable to such claims, provided that such indemnified amounts shall be reduced by any amounts recovered from insurance or third parties. This carve-out shall not extend to exemplary, punitive or consequential damages, and shall apply only to claims for which the indemnifying party had actual notice and an opportunity to defend."

Additional protective clauses to propose:
- Require prior written notice and sole defense-control rights for Redwood (with obligation to consult customer on settlements that materially affect Customer’s rights).
- Limit uncapped recovery to direct defense and settlement amounts and explicitly exclude injunctive relief and loss of business (consequential).
- Consider a modest subcap (e.g., $5M) for non-willful infringement claims, and an uncapped position only for willful third-party infringement, subject to GC-level approval.

If BrightTower insists on a fully uncapped indemnity, we should either (a) require evidence of insurance limits and an additional commercial fee, or (b) offer a mutual indemnity carve-out to avoid one-sided exposure.

I can produce a tracked-changes snippet for the MSA.

— Aditya Rao
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai
From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Commercial fallback proposals for BrightTower negotiation

Folks — quick commercial options so leadership can weigh tradeoffs: 

1) Product-first compromise (fast close): Accept Aditya’s language limiting the uncapped carve-out to defense costs and settlements, explicitly excluding consequential and punitive damages. No price change.

2) Risk-transfer (preferred for larger customers): Accept full carve-out for IP indemnity in exchange for (a) a one-time onboarding premium of $75k and (b) evidence of Customer insurance (minimum $10M coverage). Also require a 12-month termination right after final judgment.

3) Subcap approach (balanced): Uncapped for willful infringement only; for non-willful claims, apply a subcap of $5M. This keeps exposure bounded and might be acceptable to procurement.

Impacts: Option 1 gets the deal done faster but leaves Redwood more exposed in edge cases. Option 2 protects Redwood but requires Procurement sign-off and may slow the timeline. Option 3 is a durable middle ground.

Marcus — which of the above maps to our playbook for enterprise contracts in 2026? If leadership signs off on Option 3, we can present it to BrightTower this week.

Thanks — Monica

Subject: Final proposal: IP carve-out compromise and next steps

Kate / Sam — thanks for your patience while we reviewed internally. We want to keep momentum and have a fair compromise. Our proposed language (track changes attached) is summarized below: 

- IP indemnity carve-out limited to reasonable defense costs and settlements (not punitive, exemplary or consequential damages).
- Uncapped recovery permitted only for willful third-party infringement; non-willful third-party infringement damages are subject to a $5M subcap.
- Mutual obligations: Customer to provide timely notice and cooperation; Redwood to have defense control and to disclose insurance recoveries.
- If BrightTower requires full uncapped indemnity for all IP claims, we request proof of $10M insurance and a one-time commercial adjustment (onboarding fee) to be reflected in the Order Form.

We attached the redline (Redwood_MSA_Diff.docx) and a clean clause in PDF (BT-Redlines_v3.pdf) for your convenience. If this looks acceptable, please confirm and we’ll route an updated MSA and Order Form for signature.
